g3ela-25-1-teach-morph: [curious] In Chapter 1, Lucy sees a light ahead of her. Not close by. A long way off. Far! There's a word part that means far. Tele. Here's a word that's not on your list. Telegraph. Long ago, a telegraph sent messages far away, over wires. Tele, far. Graph, write. Writing sent far! Read the four words and their parts. Then tap See what was hiding, and type each word.
g3ela-25-1-teach-vocab: Be a word detective with me. Spiteful. Here's the sentence. Edmund could be spiteful, and on this occasion he was spiteful. He sneered and jeered at Lucy. One, read the sentence: he was mean to her on purpose. Two, look for word parts: spite, plus ful, full of. Three, check it. Spiteful means full of meanness. Read how we figured out the first word. Then fill in each sentence with a word from the word bank, and tap Check My Work. Last, play the matching game.
g3ela-25-1-teach-gram: [warmly] Some sentences have two parts. One part can stand alone. The other part can't. Listen. When Lucy felt something crunching. When Lucy felt something crunching, what? It can't stand alone! Add the main idea: she stooped down to feel it. When the part that can't stand alone comes first, put a comma after it. Read The Rule box, and tap Now check your thinking. Then find where each comma goes.
g3ela-25-1-teach-spell: Say this name with me. Narnia. Nar, nee, uh. Hear that last beat? It's quiet and lazy. It says uh. That lazy sound is called the schwa. Now try Edmund. Ed, mund. The u says uh! Any vowel can make the schwa. Say the eight words in the sort, and tap Now name the pattern. Then sort the words.
g3ela-25-2-teach-morph: Watch one match first. Find tele, and remember: it means far. Telework. Tele, far. Work. Telework means working far from the office, like at home. That's my match! Read the Remember box. Then tap a word, and tap what it means. Match all four words.
g3ela-25-2-teach-vocab: Here's another word from Chapter 1. Glimpse. Lucy could even catch a glimpse of the empty room. Just a quick look, through the trees. So a glimpse is a quick look. Now tap a word, then tap its meaning. Match all four.
g3ela-25-2-teach-gram: Spot the connecting word. Because it was raining, the children explored the house. Because! It starts the part that can't stand alone. Find the connecting word in each sentence, and tap Now check your thinking. Then fix the paragraph. Read slowly: the mistakes aren't all the same kind.
g3ela-25-2-teach-spell: Lazy beat hunt! Susan pulled the coats apart. Susan. Soo, zun. A lazy beat, yes! Pulled? Just one beat, no. Apart. Uh, part. Yes! Read the rule. Then tap every word with a schwa in the two sentences.
g3ela-25-2-teach-rwm: [warmly] Let's try all three parts with a different sentence from Chapter 3. There was crisp, dry snow under his feet and more snow lying on the branches of the trees. Part one, read like a reader. Edmund is in Narnia now, and it's winter. Part two, read like a writer. Lewis starts at Edmund's feet, then looks up at the trees, so you look around with him. Part three, mimic. Here's mine: There was cold, wet sand under my feet and more sand stuck to my shoes. Now it's your turn with Lewis's sentence about the house. Write one sentence in each box.
g3ela-25-3-teach-morph: Snap the parts together, like blocks. Tele. Photo. Telephoto! A telephoto lens on a camera takes pictures of things far away. Say each pair of parts out loud. Type the whole word in the box. Then tap Check My Answers.
g3ela-25-3-teach-vocab: Try each word in the blank, and keep the one that makes sense. Here's my sentence. Lucy took a quick blank back at the wardrobe. Spiteful? No. Glimpse? Yes! A glimpse is a quick look. Now pick the word that fits each sentence.
g3ela-25-3-teach-gram: Two short sentences can become one. The others did not believe Lucy. She was very unhappy. Put a joining word in front: Because the others did not believe her, comma, Lucy was very unhappy. Read the before and after. Then join the two sentences in the box.
g3ela-25-3-teach-spell: Oops! I spelled lion like this: L, I, U, N. That's how it sounds. Li, un. But that lazy uh is spelled with an o. Lion. The schwa hides the real letter. Read the rule. Then tap each card to see which vowel blurred.
g3ela-25-4-teach-morph: Eyes closed for a second. What does tele mean? Far! Keep that in your head. Here's a word that's not on the dice. Teleconference. A meeting with people far away, on a screen. Now tap Roll the Dice. Say what each word means, and tap Check My Thinking. Roll all six.
g3ela-25-4-teach-vocab: Can one word tell a whole moment? Spiteful. Edmund was spiteful when he jeered at Lucy about countries in cupboards. One word, one moment from the book. Now choose one of your words and write your own sentence.
g3ela-25-4-teach-gram: Editors read in passes. Watch me. The queens sledge had bells and edmund heard them. Pass one, capitals: The, Queen, Edmund. Pass two, apostrophes: Queen's sledge. It belongs to her. Pass three, commas: one before and. Now do your passes, and tap every word that needs fixing.
g3ela-25-4-teach-spell: Here's my roll. Tumnus. Tum, nus. Which beat is quiet and lazy? The second one. Which vowel blurs? The u! Tap Roll the dice, say the word, and find the lazy beat. Then tap Check my answer.
